scenes.title: Dimensions of Data Quality
scenes.subtitle: The measurable facets of good data
scenes.narration: Data quality is broken into distinct dimensions so each aspect can be measured and improved independently.

scenes.heading: The core dimensions
bullets: Accuracy: values reflect the real world
Completeness: no required data is missing
Timeliness: data is current enough to use
Validity: values conform to defined rules
scenes.narration: Accuracy asks whether a value matches reality, while completeness asks whether any required value is absent. Consistency checks that the same fact agrees across systems, and timeliness asks whether the data is recent enough to trust. Uniqueness guards against duplicate records, and validity confirms values obey their format and domain rules.

scenes.heading: Two easily confused dimensions

right.heading: Validity
points: Does the value follow the rules?
Compares to a defined format or domain

scenes.narration: Accuracy asks whether a value is actually true, which usually requires an external source of truth to confirm. Validity only asks whether a value obeys its defined rules, such as a date format or an allowed set of codes. A record can be perfectly valid yet completely inaccurate, so both dimensions must be measured.

scenes.heading: Checking dimensions with SQL
scenes.code:
-- Completeness: share of non-null emails
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
  COUNT(email) AS non_null_email,
  1.0 * COUNT(email) / COUNT(*) AS completeness
FROM customers;

-- Uniqueness: duplicate customer ids
SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM customers
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
scenes.narration: The first query measures completeness by comparing non-null emails to the total row count, giving a ratio we can track over time. The second query surfaces uniqueness violations by grouping on the identifier and flagging any group that appears more than once. Simple aggregate checks like these turn abstract dimensions into concrete numbers.

scenes.text: Name the dimension you care about, then measure it with a concrete rule so quality becomes trackable.
scenes.narration: Each dimension isolates one way data can be wrong, which makes problems easier to diagnose. Pick the dimensions that matter for your use case and express each as a measurable check.
